title: introduce-defaults-compiler-and-tenant-usage-prober-with-safety-gates
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a Defaults Compiler that synthesizes tenant-specific batching/caching/quant defaults from sampled telemetry and a Tenant Usage Prober which validates unit-economics and latency safety gates prior to rollout. Includes observability, a shadow-apply path, and docs/upgrade notes.
body:
Motivation: Many tenants run with conservative global defaults for batching, KV cache windowing, and quantization profiles which leaves significant cost on the table. Operators need a safe, automated way to propose tenant-specific defaults that improve unit economics without regressions. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) Defaults Compiler - a compile-time style tool that ingests sampled tenant telemetry and produces per-tenant default profiles (batch size distributions, cache TTL/kv-window hints, suggested quantization tiers) and (2) Tenant Usage Prober - a lightweight runtime probe that runs short shadow simulations against candidate defaults to validate latency and token-cost regressions before enabling them.

What this PR delivers (high level): - Defaults Compiler service (pkg/defaults/compiler) that reads tenant telemetry snapshots, runs a rule-based & simulation-backed cost synthesis, and emits JSON profile artifacts. The compiler includes safe fallthroughs and versioning so we can roll back per-tenant. - Tenant Usage Prober (pkg/prober) that executes short-lived micro-sim runs against a tenant's recent request samples to estimate latency P50/P95 and per-token cost. It returns a safety verdict (pass|soft-fail|hard-fail) and detailed diagnostics. - Safety Gate heuristics that combine regression thresholds (latency and quality tolerance), minimal throughput uplift guarantees, and a conservative adoption policy (staged canary -> tenant opt-in) - Integration points in the control plane: API to list proposed defaults, endpoint to trigger per-tenant prober runs, and a shadow-apply path for manual inspection. - Observability: metrics, traces, and a compact CSV export for cost delta analysis; new metrics include defaults.compiler.generated_profiles, prober.run_duration_seconds, and defaults.applied.safe_failures_total. - Docs and runbook: operator guide under docs/ops/defaults-compiler.md and a short tenant-facing FAQ explaining opt-in behavior.

Key design notes: - Compiler is intentionally conservative: when telemetry is sparse we prefer smaller batch improvements and avoid recommending aggressive quantization unless the prober validates output quality via evaluation traces. - Prober works on sampled recent traffic (up to 1k request samples); it runs in a sandboxed ephemeral environment using cached KV snapshots to approximate cold vs warm behavior. - All profiles are versioned and signed in the artifact store; the control plane supports staged rollouts and an immediate rollback API. - Profiling simulations use approximate kernel-latency models (existing runtime cost models updated with a small calibration table added in this PR).

Commits (summary): - 1st commit: initial compiler framework + config proto + CI scaffolding - 2nd commit: prober implementation and sandbox runner + sample collector - 3rd commit: control-plane API endpoints, artifact store wiring, and RBAC checks - 4th commit: observability, metrics, and traces - 5th commit: docs, operator runbook and integration tests - 6th commit: followups from reviews (metric names, additional unit tests, minor API ergonomics)

Files touched (high-level): - pkg/defaults/compiler/compiler.go, compiler/simulator.go, compiler/rules/*.go - pkg/prober/prober.go, prober/sandbox_runner.go, prober/sampler_adapter.go - api/handlers/defaults.go (new endpoints: /tenants/:id/defaults/propose and /tenants/:id/defaults/probe) - internal/artifacts/store.go (versioned profile artifacts) - docs/ops/defaults-compiler.md (operator guide) - docs/tenants/defaults-faq.md - tests/integration/defaults_compiler_test.go - charts/values.yaml (new feature flag defaults_compiler.enabled)

Representative code snippet (compiler rule example):

func inferBatchProfile(samples []Sample) BatchProfile {
    // compute 95th percentile length, recommend batch cap at p95*0.6 to avoid tail amplification
    seqP95 := percentile(samples.SeqLen(), 95)
    cap := int(math.Max(1, math.Floor(float64(seqP95)*0.6)))
    return BatchProfile{MaxTokensPerBatch: cap, PreferredBatchWindowMs: 12}
}

Testing and CI: - Local integration tests simulate tenants with short/long sequences and validate the compiler outputs sane defaults under sparse data. - Unit tests added for rule evaluation and prober verdict logic. - CI initially caught a flaky test in prober (sandbox teardown race) — fixed in commit 6. - All CI checks green at merge: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), e2e-smoke (pass).

Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag gated (charts.values defaults_compiler.enabled=false) 2) Enable for internal tenants only and run prober in shadow mode for a week (no automatic apply) 3) Expose proposed defaults to tenant dashboards and allow manual opt-in 4) After 2 weeks of shadow runs and manual vetting, enable staged auto-apply for low-risk tenants with strict safety gate thresholds 5) Monitor defaults.applied.* metrics and have rollback automation if soft-fail rate exceeds 2% in 24h.

Observed improvement on internal pilot (shadow-only): - Mean per-token compute cost down ~8% for chat workloads with median seq lengths < 512 - P95 latency unchanged due to conservative batch caps - Two tenants needed manual intervention because quantization suggestions produced nontrivial output artifacts; prober flagged these as hard-fail and they were quarantined for manual evaluation.

Review thread (excerpt, chronological): - Ethan Wu (reviewer): "Nice separation between compiler and prober. Please rename metric defaults.compiler.generated to defaults.compiler.generated_profiles for clarity and include tenant_id tag." - Maya (author): "Renamed metric and added tenant_id label. Also added a small CSV export for offline analysis." - Lina Fernández: "There's a missing unit test for prober verdict when samples contain mixed seq lengths (hot/cold). Can you add one?" - Maya: "Added prober verdict unit test and an integration that exercises hot/cold using cached KV snapshots (tests/integration/defaults_compiler_test.go)." - Arjun Rao: "We should be explicit about RBAC — only platform-admins can trigger a probe. Add check and documented policy." - Maya: "Added RBAC checks to api/handlers/defaults.go and updated docs/ops/defaults-compiler.md with the minimal role required."

CI notes: - First CI run: build ok, lint ok, unit-tests failed (prober teardown race) - fix committed (commit 6): add sync barrier in sandbox teardown - Second CI run: all checks green - e2e-smoke took longer due to prober warmup but passed under the CI timeout.

Backward compatibility and safety: - No breaking API changes to existing inference APIs. - Defaults are opt-in; automatic apply is feature-flag gated. - Profiles include a "safe_fallback_profile" pointer so runtime always has a conservative config to fall back to. - We added a runtime guard that rejects profiles that would lower token cost but increase P95 by >20% unless explicitly overridden by a platform admin.

Follow-ups (tracked as ENG-____): - Add a quality-eval hook for quantization candidates that runs a small regression eval comparing generated outputs to a reference set and returns a quality score — this will reduce false-positive hard-fails for quantization recommendations. - UX: Add tenant-facing UI to visualize proposed savings and allow one-click opt-in. - Telemetry: correlate defaults.applied.* with billing.total_token_cost to measure real dollar impact.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged on 2025-11-20 by Maya Patel. Post-merge run triggered the feature-flagged canary; early telemetry already visible in staging. Full rollout will follow the staged plan after internal vetting.
